items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: And I played with a, Jerry Roe Morton, but let me tell you the funny... I call him King Porter, trumpet player

ctx.x: I was just thinking about Tiny Palm, did you ever play any of his arrangements?

Yeah, head, humble, dream, all them kind of things. And I played with a, Jerry Roe Morton, but let me tell you the funny, now you're all going to laugh about this. Jerry didn't want no drinking. I went to Jerry, man, tall boy, tall boy, I call him King Porter, trumpet player, meaning I was playing first and I was playing second. So Porter hit me and said, look at you, I said, man, we can drink. I said, how are we going to drink, man? He said, I'll show you. Came into the saloon, man, we got a flash, each one's…
But he didn't fight, didn't he? He'd come on back to Chicago and he wouldn't take us out, you know. He didn't want no drinking. Strictly didn't want no drinking.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: I would call him King Porter. He was a trumpet player, too. He played first trumpet. Me and him used to bum together.

ctx.x: Can you tell us something more about Jelly? Who was in the band when you...

Well, there's one fellow I can remember, because me and him used to bum together. I would call him King Porter. He was a trumpet player, too. He played first trumpet. Me and him used to bum together. Now, the other fellows, really, I don't forgot the names and things, you know. I really have.
